meta.probability_formula: probability = (2*k_recent + k_older + 1) / (2*n_recent + n_older + 2); k = papers containing the topic, n = papers; recent = 2026-27. Primary 'probability' uses BCSE308L FAT papers only (n_recent=0, n_older=11). 'probability_all_papers' uses CAT1/CAT2/FAT papers whose measured syllabus window covers the topic's module ({'CAT1': ['M1', 'M2', 'M3'], 'CAT2': ['M3', 'M4', 'M5'], 'FAT': ['M1', 'M2', 'M3', 'M4', 'M5', 'M6', 'M7']}).
meta.tag_agreement_detail: 13 questions re-read (BCSE308L-FAT-F2-2025-2026 Q1a-Q6iv, pages 1-2): text 13/13, type 13/13, bloom 11/13, scenario 9/13; pooled 33/39 = 0.85.
meta.small_n_warning: No 2026-27 BCSE308L FAT exists (n_recent = 0 for the FAT formula). Use the 2026-27 CAT and sister-FAT columns as recency signal.
meta.fat_blueprint_observed: 10 x 10 FAT in 9 of 11 (C2 2022-23 and A1 2025-26 printed 11-13 numbered questions); all 7 modules in 10 of 11. Typical order Q1 M1 (layers/topologies), Q2 M2 (switching/delay), Q3-Q4 M3 (error detection, MAC, flow control), Q4-Q6 M4 (IPv4 subnetting, fragmentation), Q6-Q7 M5 (routing), Q7-Q9 M6 (congestion, TCP), Q8-Q10 M7 (application layer). Your slot letter's last FATs (F1, F2 2025-26) moved M3 to Q9-Q10. No 2026-27 BCSE308L FAT in the corpus; 2026-27 evidence = CAT-1/CAT-2 C1 and C2 plus sister FATs BACSE203 B1 and CBS3001 C2.
